I am a Christian. To be specific I am strictly non-Denominational. Why? Because I agree with the point about the division religion can cause. I don't think religion should be done away with since we as a flawed species will find a way to take anything to far(a talk for another time). But I definitely learned in history about the conflict between the protestant and catholic churches and decided to just go by the basic outline of Christianity as opposed to claiming affiliation to specific denomination. Focusing on the values of forgiveness, humility, love etc as opposed to ''my church is the only true church!''

Now while I do have bias in terms of being brought up in a household that attended church irregularly, at the bare minimum I am a theist. I not only believe in a higher power, but one that does interact with the universe. I definitely am doing more research on Christianity in general, including the Old Testament. I am currently reading ''Is God a Moral Monster'' by Paul Copan.

I do respect the opinions of others, but one thing that irks me is saying that God doesn't exist because there is evil in the world. One it seems to be more of an emotional argument since logically the fact that acts of moral evil exist doesn't have any bearing on whether or not a higher power exist. Two, some say that the universe isn't fined tuned since it's not perfect(hurricanes, tsunamis, disease, etc). But here's the thing:

What if the universe isn't mean to be perfect? Now I know you are probably familiar with the free will argument but allow me to expand on that. Firstly like most people you've probably had an experience in your life that made you feel sad,angry,etc. Now after that experience was there a positive experience that made you feel happy, joyful etc? If so would you say that one of the reasons it felt so good was because of the negative experience?

Basically what I'm trying to say is that the way I see it God didn't make the world imperfect just for the sake of free will, but also so that positive and negative traits could be experienced based off the choices we make. How would we know what it's like to be strong(physically and mentally) if we were never challenged? How could there be courage is there's no need to overcome fear? How can there be ambition in a world where there's no dreams to achieve, obstacles to overcome and no discoveries to be made? There's no need to do those things since there would be no ambition or need. How could there be victory without defeat? Like the saying goes, ''Victory is sweetest when you've tasted defeat.'' A world with no free will would basically be like Lois Lowry's book ''The Giver''.

I at the very least do believe that there is something behind our universe that does interact with this world. I believe in Christianity without a denomination as a guide to go by in life but am researching it more because I do feel there coul be more than meets the eye. I also feel the biggest problem is black and white thinking. It seems we appy that too much to everything, things must be this way or the other with no inbetween. Sometimes that's the case, but then you have the idea that belief in God and evolution are mutually exclusive. But why couldn't God use evolution as a mechanism to bring mankind to the point we are now? What if the Bible is more allegorical than we thought and survival of the fittest could have something to do with the Fall nd mankind now lives in a fallen world?

But what do you guys think about there being a personal higher power, and the argument of God not existing at all because moral evil is committed?
